importance_ranking.reason: Significant visual variation across sub-types — single isolation cabin, multi-bed ward block, and container-based mobile hospital are visually distinct configurations. Buyers use the image to identify the correct product type before reading any specification; wrong configuration = immediate skip.

Bed capacity, negative pressure provision, insulation type, and HVAC configuration are non-negotiable clinical shortlisting criteria. Without matching specs, institutional buyers cannot evaluate compliance or fit for their facility requirements.

importance_ranking.brand_important_reason: No dominant brand with buyer recall in this category — market is fragmented across regional prefab manufacturers; buyers search by spec, certification, and track record rather than manufacturer name.
importance_ranking.reason: Government and institutional buyers run vendor qualification checks on ISO certification, NABH-compliant construction experience, and past government supply track record. Supplier credentials are evaluated during shortlisting but specs carry equal or greater weight at initial engagement.

Price varies substantially with bed count, built type, HVAC configuration, and negative pressure provision — buyers discover and compare across spec tiers during search. Listed price is a budget entry point; final price is always project-negotiated, particularly for government tender procurement.

importance_ranking.unit_note: Custom panel-build configurations may be quoted per sq ft, but complete ready-to-deploy ward units are universally quoted per piece. Unit is implied by the product for finished ward structures.
importance_ranking.reason: Per piece is the dominant and universally understood unit for complete prefabricated isolation ward units. No buyer questions whether a finished ward structure is sold per piece.

top_configurator_specs.reason: Bed count defines the entire structural scale of the ward — a 1-bed isolation cabin and a 30-bed ward are non-interchangeable products with the largest single price delta in this category.

Construction methodology (Container vs Panel Build vs Modular) is non-interchangeable — each represents a different structural system, deployment context, and price tier that buyers cannot substitute for one another.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Healthcare facility compliance (NABH, National Building Code) requires specific fire resistance ratings for patient ward structures — buyers in government procurement specify this as a mandatory eligibility criterion.

The facing material of sandwich panels (GI, MS, Stainless Steel, FRP) determines antimicrobial surface performance, durability in clinical environments, and cost — a primary differentiator for hospital-grade vs standard isolation wards.
Institutional and government buyers require ISO 9001 certification and NABH-compliant construction credentials as a vendor qualification gate before shortlisting suppliers.

top_rfq_specs.reason: Bed count directly communicates the scale of the buyer's requirement — sellers immediately determine whether they can supply the requested ward size and quote accurately.

Panel material (PUF vs Rockwool vs Cement) defines the structural and thermal specification tier — sellers need this to confirm product eligibility for the buyer's clinical and compliance requirements.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Sellers need to know the clinical application (ICU, COVID ward, quarantine, isolation, screening) to confirm the required HVAC configuration, negative pressure provision, and compliance standard — without this, sellers cannot determine fit or price accurately.
